text:
olivia: FYI — canary p95 CPU and tail-latency jumped ~3x after roll 2026-03-22 22:40 UTC. Noticed on /v1/generate-cfg route. Thinking we should do a manual unwind; auto-revert didn't fire.

deploybot: Deploybot detected metric drift on canary slice (slice_id=canary-17). Autorevert policy: p95>1200ms for 5m required 3m window — current p95=900ms but tail 99.9 spike >2500ms so condition not met. Suggest manual hold. :warning:

sasha: Can you paste the top metrics and recent traces? Need to understand whether this is a sustained regression or a noisy outlier.

olivia: quick snippets —
```
route: /v1/generate-cfg
canary_slice: canary-17
p95_pre: 320ms
p95_now: 940ms
p999_now: 2600ms
error_rate_now: 0.2% (unchanged)
```
traces show a few long tails concentrated in requests with seq_len>4096 and using quantize=true path.

ben: If quantize flag is the common link, can we rollback just the flag (feature flag) instead of full version revert? Safer if release was config-only.

maria: Release notes draft in case we need a customer outbound: "We briefly observed higher tail latency for long-sequence requests after a performance tuning change; mitigation in progress; no data loss." I'll have a concise customer note ready once we decide.

emily: Oncall agrees: manual rollback to previous config recommended while we dig. Can we slice traffic to 10% of canary (fast rollback path) while we validate?

olivia: I'm +1 for targeted rollback of quantize flag on canary-17 and a small staged rollback (10% -> 50% -> full) if it stabilizes. Manual trigger command: `deployctl rollback-config --route /v1/generate-cfg --flag quantize --target-slice canary-17 --to false`

deploybot: Acknowledged. Manual rollback approval required from eng-release lead. Will enqueue command for operator execution. Estimated time to apply: ~45s for flag propagation.

sasha: Approving manual rollback. Ben, please stand by to patch the config-uploader so the flag change doesn't reapply on next roll. Olivia, coordinate with QA for quick smoke tests (seq_len > 4096, quantize=false).

ben: On it. Will add a short-lived override at infra layer: `config-store:set /services/gateway/flags/quantize false --ttl 1h` so it doesn't persist across full deploys.

oncall-bot: Incident marker created — incident/2026-03-22-canary-tail-latency. Pager duty: oncall (emily) notified.

maria: Drafted outbound for impacted customers (internal review): "We saw intermittent high latency on long-sequence requests; we've paused the new quantization config on canary and are monitoring. No customer-facing errors observed. We'll provide an update in 30 minutes."

emily: Executing manual rollback now. Will post when finishes.

deploybot: Command executed by emily at 2026-03-22 22:48:10 UTC. Flag propagation complete. Observability: starting new window.

olivia: New window p95=330ms, p999 falling to ~600ms. Initial signs good. Keeping canary at 10% for 15m.

sasha: Great. Next actions: 1) Ben to add one-hour override (done), 2) Olivia + QA run longer stress for seq_len>8k, 3) Deploybot config change: adjust autorevert policy to include p999 threshold for tail-latency signal, 4) Release notes update.

ben: Override pushed. Quick smoke passed locally.

emily: Oncall will keep watch for 45m. If stable, plan to roll change to main with quantize=false and include in release notes as revert of experiment.

maria: Updated release note entry and shared draft with comms.

sasha: After we've validated, let's also schedule a short postmortem to review why autorevert didn't consider p999. Add a follow-up ticket to infra.

olivia: filing ticket now: INFRA-7321 "autorevert: include p999 tail-latency in canary triggers". Assigning to infra.

oncall-bot: Incident updated: mitigation applied, monitoring. Next update due 23:10 UTC.

emily: Thanks all. Tagging PMs @sara and @kevin for visibility. :eyes: 

maria: Sending customer note in 5. Will reference incident id.

sasha: Closing loop — after stable window we'll unpin override and bake a permanent config fix. Good catch and quick ops. :thumbsup:
